terms.hint: Seeing it from the customer's side
Hear the full problem before replying
Pass it to someone who can help
Only commit to what you can deliver

questions.q: An angry customer is venting. What's your first move?
options: Listen fully and acknowledge their frustration
questions.explain: Let them be heard first — acknowledgement defuses far more than a policy quote.

questions.q: Best way to say no to a request you can't meet?
options: Explain why, then offer the closest alternative you can
questions.explain: A clear reason plus a helpful alternative keeps the relationship intact.

questions.q: You promised a callback by 2pm but can't make it. You should…
options: Say nothing and hope they forget
Proactively let them know and set a new time
questions.explain: Proactive honesty about a slip builds more trust than silence ever could.

questions.q: What turns a complaint into loyalty?
options: A fast, fair resolution and genuine care
A long apology with no fix
questions.explain: Customers remember how well you put it right far more than the original mistake.

questions.q: When should you escalate an issue?
options: When it's beyond your authority or expertise to resolve well
Only after the customer demands it
questions.explain: Escalate when someone else can genuinely resolve it better — that's good service, not failure.

options: Acknowledges the impact and what you'll do next
questions.explain: Own the impact and state the fix — that's an apology that lands.

steps: Follow up to confirm it's fixed
